summary: The proposal presents a well-developed technical concept with detailed sub-objectives and a clear schedule, but it has a critical structural gap (missing Abstract) and numerous major issues including pervasive first-person "I" usage (~15 instances), a solution statement misplaced in the Problem section, inconsistent role terminology, a non-peer-reviewed bibliography entry, an underspecified figure caption, and a missing AI review confirmation sentence. Addressing these issues—particularly the Abstract, the first-person rewrite, and the structural/citation fixes—would bring the proposal into submittable shape.

findings.title: Missing Abstract section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an Abstract section. The document transitions directly from the title page (Page 1) to Section 1 'Introduction' (Page 2). The guidelines require an Abstract of 1/3 to 1/2 page as the first content section after the title page.

locations.quote: No Abstract section present between title page and Section 1 Introduction

findings.title: Problem section contains a proposed solution
findings.description: The last sentence of the Problem section proposes a specific solution (a self-service platform arming the Keycloak workflow engine with an expiry date). The Problem section must only describe problems and their negative consequences, not present solutions or alternatives. This sentence should be removed from the Problem section (it may belong in Motivation or Objectives instead).

locations.quote: A self-service platform that arms the workflow engine of Keycloak with an expiry date at grant time would end this accumulation.

findings.title: Pervasive use of first-person singular "I"
findings.description: The guidelines state to avoid "I" and use "we" sparingly, only for the thesis approach. The student uses "I" in approximately 15 instances across the Objective, sub-objective, and Schedule sections. Restructure sentences to name the thesis/work as the subject (e.g., "The platform will…", "This work stores…") or use "we" sparingly for the thesis approach only. The AI Transparency statement (page 10) is a natural exception where first person is expected.

findings.title: Objective 4.2 uses a double-verb formulation
findings.description: The objective heading and bullet point 'Design and implement connectors with expiry' combine two verbs ('Design' and 'implement'), which the guidelines explicitly prohibit. The student should choose one verb (e.g., 'Implement connectors with expiry' or 'Design connectors with expiry') to keep the objective as a single action.

4.2 Design and Implement Connectors with Expiry

findings.title: Inconsistent terminology: "maintainer" vs. "resource owner"
findings.description: The role of the person who reviews access requests and looks after a project is called "maintainer" (or "Maintainer") throughout most of the document (Problem, Motivation, Objective 4.1, Figure 1, Schedule), but in section 4.3 the same role is referred to as "resource owner" (twice). The term should be unified to "maintainer" (or, if "resource owner" is the intended term, it should be introduced explicitly in an earlier section and used consistently thereafter).

findings.title: Non-peer-reviewed source in bibliography: Keycloak documentation guide
findings.description: The entry [Key26] 'Keycloak Server Administration Guide' is an online documentation guide, not a peer-reviewed publication. Per the guidelines, internet sources and documentation links must appear as footnotes, not as bibliography entries. This entry should be removed from the Bibliography and converted to a footnote wherever it is cited in the text (Section 1.2). The remaining 12 entries are all peer-reviewed, so the 6–8 minimum is still met.

findings.title: Figure 2 caption is too short and generic
findings.description: The caption for Figure 2 reads only "System Architecture" (two words). The guidelines require captions to be long and informative, describing what the figure shows, which components are involved, how they connect, and what the key relationships represent. Compare this with Figure 1's caption, which is a full paragraph. The caption for Figure 2 should at minimum name the components (mgmt-ui, mgmt-api, Keycloak, Slack, GitHub, Linux host, PostgreSQL, ldap-bridge), describe the key connections (OIDC login, admin API, bot token, LDAP), and explain the architectural pattern.

locations.quote: Figure 2: System Architecture

findings.title: Missing review confirmation sentence in AI transparency statement
findings.description: The AI transparency statement is missing the required review confirmation sentence. The guidelines mandate a sentence confirming that the author has carefully checked all AI-generated text, with language similar to: "I have carefully checked all texts created with these tools to ensure that they are correct and make sense." No such sentence appears in the statement, which ends after the table without any concluding confirmation of review.
